children.name: More productive and competitive business ecosystem designed to improve people's standards of living and well-being
children.description: Outcome 1: The small size of Caribbean economies and the shortfalls in innovation and digital transformation influence the level of productivity and overall competitiveness of the region. Achieving sustainable transformation of the Caribbean business environment requires the enhanced productivity of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises’ (MSMEs), which can only be achieved by creating a more productive and competitive business ecosystem. Involving  the private sector  early on in the transformation process is  essential given its  increasingly important role in achieving inclusive sustainable development, including through public-private partnership. Involving the private sector  early on in the transformation process is  essential given its  increasingly important role in achieving inclusive sustainable development, including through public-private partnership.  An important element to this area is the establishment of innovative and sustainable financial architecture that can enable MSME access to financial markets. The United Nations can play an important interlocuter role between private-sector financiers, the public sector and other (international) financial institutions.

framework.name: Equality, Well-Being and Leaving No One Behind

children.name: National governments and regional institutions use relevant data to design and adopt laws and policies to eliminate discrimination, address structural inequalities and ensure the advancement of those left furthest behind
children.description: In order to reduce inequalities and enhance people’s health and well-being, legislative and policy frameworks should eliminate discrimination, support equality, address the social and environmental determinants of health, provide for universal coverage and access to quality social and health services and help those furthest behind to claim their rights, ensuring they are not left behind.  Strengthened capabilities for data collection and analysis, including on application of the principles of a human rights-based approach to data and indicators (HRBAD) , and strong and harmonized data collection system are required.  These will support evidence-based policy and planning processes that should employ rights-based and gender-responsive approaches and an attention to the multidimensional nature of vulnerabilities.

Caribbean countries manage natural resources and ecosystems to strengthen their resilience and enhance the resilience and prosperity of the people and communities that depend on them.
children.description: Caribbean economies are highly dependent on the region’s natural resources and biodiverse ecosystems, both of which provide key services and co-benefits to people and communities. Economic resilience is, however, a critical challenge for the region in the face of environmental, climate and disaster risks, which collectively destroy natural resources and limit the region’s transformative capacity. The challenges of desertification, forest management, biodiversity loss and climate change are interrelated and need to be collectively addressed to achieve sustainable development in the Caribbean.  Both marine and terrestrial biodiversity conservation are acute issues requiring prioritization to ensure the sustainable use of ecosystems. Nature-based solutions that tackle overexploitation and address pollution and waste management should be optimised with specific attention provided to food and water security, a challenge that was further evidenced during the COVID-19 crisis.

projects.name: St. Lucia Southeast Coast Project - Integrated Ecosytem Management and Restoration of Forests
projects.description: The GEF-6 (#9406) Project The project enables sustainable economic development of the South East Coast by maintaining healthy ecosystems, sustainable livelihoods and securing global environmental benefits (GEBs). The Project promotes a more cohesive, ecosystem-based approach to development, including interrelated development planning and restoration of ecosystem services, and the establishment of sustainable management and natural resource use best practices. The objectives are change patterns of degradation on SLU's Southeast Coast, reduce impoverishment of local populations and loss of global environmental goods. The Project 3 Components: 1) Ecosystem Management - establishing effective ecosystems management mechanisms; 2) Rehabilitated Landscapes - supported through improved mechanisms for land use planning and collaborative investment decision-making; 3) Sustainable Livelihoods - identifying economic opportunities, incentives and livelihoods for primary natural resources users. Key national IP is the Department of Sustainable Development. The Project has been extended to 31 March 2027 with a total budget of $4,428,145.

projects.name: Antigua and Barbuda Sustainable Low-Emission Island Mobility Project
projects.description: The Project, "Supporting Antigua and Barbuda's Sustainable Low-Emission Island Mobility and transition" (GEF-7 #10281) addresses priorities to transition Antigua and Barbuda's transportation and energy sectors towards a low-carbon trajectory. Total allocation is $3,245,000. As a small island developing state (SIDS), Antigua and Barbuda’s greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions represent just 0.0015% of the world’s total. However, the country’s per capita GHG emissions are higher than those of Spain and France. Antigua and Barbuda’s biggest challenge is the energy sector, which, due to fossil fuel combustion activities, accounts for 76% of the country’s total emissions. These two sectors rely almost entirely on imported petroleum-based fuels. Electricity generation is responsible for close to 40% of total GHG emissions generated from heavy fuel oil thermal power plants and experiences high distribution grid inefficiencies. As a result, the emission intensity per MWh of the electricity consumed is around 1000 kg of CO2 per MWh generated, almost double the global average. The transport sub-sector is similarly problematic, with road transport accounting for more than 20% of total national GHG emissions. Under business as usual (BAU) conditions overall emissions are expected to rise considerably over the next decade, primarily due to increases in electricity demand and growth in individual transport usage. BAU estimations indicate that the private vehicle fleet could grow at an annual rate of 6.5% per year.  Project activities will put in motion the transformation of both the power and transport sectors of Antigua and Barbuda, transitioning these from the current scenario of fossil fuel dependence to a future where low-carbon and climate resilient technologies are predominant. The Project will strengthen and inform political and public support for the uptake of low-carbon and climate-resilient electric transport and power generation systems. Activities include: reducing technological, financial and modal barriers through technical assistance and investment in pilot projects; building local capacity in related areas; and implementing regulations, policies and standards to secure a sustainable transition into the future and avoid potential environmental contamination. The Project has been extended to 30 April 2027

projects.name: Achieving a rapid decarbonization of the energy sector in Saint Kitts and Nevis
projects.description:
The GEF-7 (#10856) Project supports the country in accelerating decarbonization by transitioning towards a highly ambitious target of 100% renewable energy generation. To achieve this, the Government of St. Kitts and Nevis intends to harness renewable energy sources, namely geothermal, solar, wind and waste. It also aims to reduce consumption through achieving 100% high energy e\0fficiency in public buildings. The electrical grid accounts for approximately 65% of the country’s emissions and is therefore the target with the highest potential – especially considering that a decarbonized electricity grid is also a pre-condition for the
future decarbonization of the transport sector. Although Saint Kitts & Nevis' overall emissions are minute (203,036 tCO in 2016), its per capita emissions are relatively large. Electricity generation is responsible for close to 65% of total GHG emissions, as the country relies almost entirely on diesel generators.

A key challenge is to build a comprehensive enabling environment, that can support St. Kitts and Nevis to manage and achieve a transition to decarbonization in a controlled and economically, socially and environmentally viable manner. The GEF incremental logic is that through its \0investment, St. Kitts and Nevis will be able to build upon existing investment to address barriers to decarbonization and achieve its ambitious climate targets. The Project budget is $3,318,995 and is scheduled for completion by 31 December 2027.

projects.name: Barbados Coastal Fisheries Project
projects.description: The passage of Hurricane Beryl on 1 July 2024 resulted in significant losses and damages to Barbados’ coastal assets and infrastructure. Some of the most significant impacts were felt by the Oistins Fisheries complex south of Bridgetown and the Barbados Fisheries Complex in Bridgetown where most damages were concentrated. The Barbados Fisheries Complex comprises the primary harbour facility for the fishing fleet, fish landing facilities, and a market. It is estimated that more than 200 vessels owned by local fishers suffered damage. These impacts reveal significant vulnerabilities, particularly related to a lack of a natural sheltered harbour and safe harbour facilities. To comprehensively address the full scope of the challenge outlined above is beyond the scope of this project and would likely require broader and more sustained support. However, this project aims to provide tangible and catalytic early recovery by focusing on strategic reinstatement and resilience upgrades of select physical infrastructures and assets including equipment to facilitate business continuity and resilient operations, complemented and enabled by targeted capacity building, and strategic partnerships.  The project’s design is guided by the principle that early recovery interventions that enable ‘building back better’ by incorporating increased resilience and enhancing disaster preparedness will both alleviate present impacts from Hurricane Beryl as well as reduce the risk of the adverse effects of future natural disasters on the local fishing community in Barbados.  USD $2.93 Million will be deployed in a targeted manner over the course of one year to contribute to resilient reconstruction focused on materials, equipment and installations that can be readily procured and installed and will be complementary and/or catalytic with broader reconstruction and resilience building efforts. It is expected that the project will directly impact 100 boat owners, 300 fishers, more than 150 fish vendor/processors and will improve the skills of 100 industry stakeholders including the Barbados National Union of Fisherfolk Organization (BARNUFO). The entire fishing industry with a participation of 6000  persons stands to benefit from the improvement in disaster preparedness protocols and safer and more resilient facilities. The project will also have a positive indirect benefit to restaurants, domestic consumers (close to 100,000 households) and the vital tourism sector. The tourism sector comprises close to 156 properties of which 64 are hotels; stay over arrivals of 636,606 and cruise arrivals 441,677 people recorded in 2024 .  The proposal will form part of a wider Government of Barbados Fisheries Recovery Plan for the repair and replacement of vessels, rehabilitation of the marine based components of the Bridgetown Fisheries Complex (breakwater, finger pier, and slip way); rehabilitation of landing facilities and coastal protection along with capacity building in disaster management, and is complementary to initiatives funded by other international partners such as the World Bank.

projects.name: TTO Ethical Recruitment and Work Permit Support in Aruba
projects.description:
Work Permit Support:
1. IOM Aruba will provide additional capacity and technical support to the Government of Aruba to undocumented migrants with work permit procedures, including for their family members, as allowed in the new policy. Additionally, beneficiaries requiring CBI assistance in order to access permits will receive a small grant. The level of subsidy for the permits will depend on the beneficiaries' vulnerability, assessed using predefined criteria. Importantly, the financial responsibility for these permits will not rest solely on IOM; private sector partners will also contribute to the costs.  
2. IOM Aruba will provide targeted support to the Government of Aruba for the implementation of the new work permit policy, enhancing the government's capacity through technical inputs and assistance. This support aims to streamline processes, improve policy implementation, and ensure that the work permit system effectively addresses the needs of both migrants and the host community. The assistance will include in-kind technical support, such as providing resources, tools, and specialized expertise to facilitate the policy rollout. Additionally, IOM Aruba will offer technical assistance, including capacity-building activities, training sessions, and advisory services to government officials. This collaborative effort is designed to strengthen the government's capacity to manage work permits efficiently, foster economic inclusion, and promote a more organized and responsive labor market in Aruba.

Ethical Recruitment Programme:
The IOM Ethical Recruitment Program aims to promote fair and responsible hiring practices by working closely with employers and recruiters to ensure that labor migration is safe, transparent, and equitable. The program focuses on preventing exploitation and abuse of workers by promoting principles such as no recruitment fees for job seekers, clear employment terms, and respect for workers’ rights. Through training, capacity building, and guidelines, the program helps private sector partners adhere to ethical standards that protect both migrants and employers, fostering a fair and sustainable labor market that benefits all parties involved.

projects.name: Global Biodiversity Framework Early Action Support (GBF-EAS)
projects.description:
The recent “Little Book on Investing in Nature” estimates the global annual biodiversity financing gap at US$700 billion. The CBD Panel of Experts on Resource Mobilization highlighted that 
implementation of the new biodiversity targets under the Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) will require additional financial resources, increased resource efficiency, and a reduction of biodiversity-harmful financial flows. Reducing the biodiversity finance gap can only be achieved through transformative change across 
economies and society.
To develop a clear picture of how to achieve the targets of the CBD’s GBF, a detailed assessment of the policy and institutional national context, a biodiversity expenditures review and financial needs are required as well as development and implementation of finance plans. CBD Parties face the following key barriers to sustainable financing of nature-positive policies and practices: (a) limited awareness, coordination, and capacity among national stakeholders to address gaps in biodiversity financing; (b) insufficient knowledge and systematic (c) lack of systematic measurement and reporting 
of the negative impacts of finance contributing to biodiversity loss; (d) biodiversity finance needs are imprecisely defined and poorly understood; (e) limited knowledge, use and mainstreaming of country-specific biodiversity finance solutions; and (f) limited exchange and uptake of global best practices in the sustainable 
financing of biodiversity.

Given the need for a comprehensive and multi-stakeholder strategic approach to resource mobilization, Target 19 requests all countries to develop national biodiversity finance plans (BFPs). These BFPs should assess the root causes of biodiversity loss, identify national biodiversity finance gaps, and articulate strategies on how to reduce the gaps through a suite of finance solutions aimed at reducing flow of resources that cause harm to biodiversity; generating additional resources; and enhancing the effectiveness and efficiency of resource use. To respond to this need and based on the experience of UNDP’s Biodiversity Finance Initiative (BIOFIN) and other relevant methodologies, this project aims to support a global programme that will establish a transformative 
process for biodiversity finance in all participating eligible countries, involving all relevant stakeholders such as Ministries of Finance and Environment, and the private and financial sectors through a socially and gender-inclusive approach. The project will support countries in baseline diagnostics, capacity and institutional strengthening, and developing finance plans to mobilize resources at scale to implement the GBF.

projects.name: Sustainable Land Management in the Commonwealth of Dominica  (GEF-6, #9667)
projects.description: Land degradation is a major concern in Dominica, driven mainly by development pressures, livelihoods challenges, and meteorological events in a physically vulnerable landscape. Despite the importance of agriculture for Dominica’s economy, the mountainous terrain of the country and variations in soil quality mean that only 20% of the land is suitable for agriculture (although an estimated 24.7% of the land is being farmed) due to erosion risks and potential water saturation during heavy rainfall. The island's central mountainous zone remains heavily forested and provides critical water catchment services as well as most of the protected landscapes in the country, while lower elevations continue to lose forest cover and is being degraded. The Project’s objective is the establishment of landscape level planning, information and coordination frameworks to support sustainable agriculture and sustainable watershed management in Dominica. The Project commenced in 2018, has experience delays and disruption from the COVID-19 Pandemic and has been extended several times. Project expenditures between 2018-2021 = $490,256. Project is in closure stage.

projects.name: Enhancing Smart Sustainable Agriculture and Agro-Processing for Climate Resilience in Dominica: Phase 1
projects.description:
The project, titled "Enhancing Climate Smart Sustainable Agriculture and Agro-Processing for Climate Resilience in Dominica – Phase 1" ESSAA-1, is Phase 1 of a comprehensive initiative that addresses critical challenges faced by Dominica's agricultural sector. The project seeks during this 1st phase to develop effective gender responsive mitigation and adaptation measures, by enhancing resilience to climate change in supporting sustainable agriculture and strengthening agro-processing. The project follows the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, supporting specifically the attainment of the following Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) identified as priority for the MASE-CARICOM cooperation: SDG 5, 6,7, 9, 12, 13, 15, 17. The project also aligns with the objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

The project aims to support the sustainable and integrated management of resources; in particular water. The project offers gender responsive capacity-strengthening programs in climate-smart agriculture to empower vegetable farmers in the Morne Prosper community, enabling them to tackle climate-related challenges and improve food and water security. Gender sensitive stakeholder engagement is a core component, ensuring that the project aligns with local needs and priorities.

projects.description:
Level of UNICEF support to Government to improve the availability and quality of child-related and quality of child-related Sustainable Development Goal indicators is being implemented. The extent is an index will be measured by the following indicators: 
1) Country Office has collaborated with the government to conduct a full Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) or any other household survey which includes at least 20 child-related SDG indicators. 
2) Extent to which the Country Office supported (technically and/or financially) the strengthening of national routine/administrative data systems of individual sectors as well as cross sectoral interoperability.
3) Extent to which the Country Office supported (technically and/or financially) government efforts to strengthen the overall national statistical system regarding data about children, in alignment with national statistical master plans, or the National Strategy for the Development of Statistics during the reporting year
 4) Extent to which the Country Office supported the inclusion of statistical data for children in planning documents prepared by the government (including sectoral and sub-national ones) and Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) of SDG implementation during the reporting year 
5) Extent to which the Country Office supported good data governance standards regarding data for children (including Responsible Data for Children principles, Ethical Framework for Evidence Generation, Data Quality Framework) and the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics.

projects.name: TTO: ASYCUDA Extended Digitalisation of Customs Clearance in Trinidad and Tobago
projects.description: In October 2025, the Ministry of Finance and the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) signed a new partnership to modernise the country’s customs operations through the Automated System for Customs Data (ASYCUDA) marking a major milestone in efforts to improve trade facilitation, strengthen revenue collection, and create a more transparent, efficient customs environment. Developed by UNCTAD, ASYCUDA is a globally recognised customs management system that automates trade and transport procedures in line with international standards. The 18-month, USD 1.75 million project will deploy the latest ASYCUDA World modules and the ASYHUB data exchange platform at the Customs and Excise Division to expand paperless processing, reduce clearance times and costs, and provide real-time trade data. The systems will enhance risk management, cargo control, and interoperability among port and cargo operators, while enabling pre-arrival and pre-departure processing to expedite legitimate trade. Improved data analytics will also support evidence-based policymaking, strengthen border security, and reduce revenue losses—advancing a more efficient and competitive trade environment.

projects.name: TTO – UNODC Global Programme on Cybercrime: Trinidad and Tobago has increased capacity to identify, investigate, prosecute and adjudicate online child sexual exploitation and trafficking in persons facilitated by information and communications technologies.
projects.description:
UNODC’s Global Programme on Cybercrime is designed to respond flexibly to identified needs in developing countries by supporting Member States to prevent and combat cybercrime in a holistic manner.  The key objectives of this programme are:
•	Increased efficiency and effectiveness in the investigation, prosecution and adjudication of cybercrime, especially online child sexual exploitation and abuse, within a strong human-rights framework;
•	Efficient and effective long-term whole-of-government response to cybercrime, including national coordination, data collection and effective legal frameworks, leading to a sustainable response and greater deterrence;
•	Strengthened national and international communication between government, law enforcement and the private sector with increased public knowledge of cybercrime risks.

In 2022, UNODC launched the Project “Strengthening Trinidad and Tobago capacities to effectively prevent and counter online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes” under the Global Cybercrime Project of UNODC. This project is funded by the Government of Canada and will be implemented until December 2024. The project aims to enhance the capacity of Trinidad and Tobago to identify, investigate, prosecute, adjudicate and prevent online child sexual exploitation and trafficking in persons facilitated by information and communications technologies.
Capacity building includes:
•	Cybercrime and digital evidence basics, proactive online investigations: using specialized platforms, such as CPS or ICACCOPS, to detect in real time the distribution of online child sexual exploitation material;
•	Train the trainer workshop in reactive online investigations: using platforms, such as the CyberTipline reporting mechanism, to receive reports from foreign technology companies on cases of online child sexual exploitation;
•	Open-source intelligence applied in investigating online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes;
•	Identifying and handling digital evidence;
•	Criminal investigations involving the dark web, cryptocurrencies, for example.

Likewise, the Project will also facilitate the provision of specialized equipment for identifying, acquiring, analysing, and preserving digital evidence for the units responsible for investigating online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes, as well as activities to support to Civil Society, prevention, and cooperation.
In 2022, the following activities were conducted:
-	17th October 2022- Project Launch “Strengthening Trinidad and Tobago capacities to effectively prevent and counter online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes”. Organized by UNODC in collaboration with: Attorney General and Minister of Legal Affairs of T&T; Commissioner of Police; CARICOM IMPACS, International Centre for Missing & Exploited Children (ICMEC), and the donor Canada. With the participation of 15 Institutions, NGOs and UN Agencies.

Organized by UNODC in collaboration with International Centre for Missing & Exploited Children (ICMEC), with the participation of 16 Institutions, NGOs and UN Agencies.

projects.name: REG Caribbean BluEFin - Caribbean Blue Economy Financing Project
projects.description:
The GEF-7 (#10782) Project also known as the "Caribbean Blue Economy Financing Project” is implemented in The Bahamas (Dominican Republic), Grenada, St. Lucia, and St. Vincent and the Grenadines. The objective is to create and strengthen nature-based Blue Economy opportunities and approaches in the Caribbean through innovative financing mechanisms, and targets The Bahamas,  Dominican Republic,  Grenada,  St. Lucia,  St. Vincent and Grenadines. As the concepts of “Blue Economy” and “Blue Businesses” are in early stages of development in the insular Caribbean region, the BluEFin Project aims to facilitate coordination of activities directed at identifying sources of economic value in the marine and coastal areas and facilitate development of long-term solutions and sustainable financing mechanisms. The coordination will efficiently consider the best use of Blue Economy opportunities for conservation financing mechanisms, marrying 2 core international commitments. The Project also supports Caribbean countries by building on and delivering the GEF Caribbean Large Marine Ecosystem (CLME+), Strategic Action Programmmes' (SAP) project implementation targets. The Project brings together public and private sector partners of the Caribbean Sustainable Finance Architecture (CSFA) to identify feasible Caribbean-based regional and national Financing Mechanisms (FMs).  Component #3 develops a Blue Economy Hub; while Component 4 supports a Community of learning, and strengthening of regional networks on the value of Blue Economy in Caribbean regional financing and development. Support will also be provided for high level discussions among Caribbean Leaders on the Caribbean's 30x30 Vision for Ocean Governance (as a follow on to the Caribbean Challenge Initiative with its 2020 target) and CBF will promote regional FMs as a vehicle and targeting NGOs and the private sector. The implementation partner is the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund.

Component 1 of the Project applies Blue Economy principles to develop at least three regional Ocean finance mechanisms that generate long‑term, reliable funding for marine and coastal biodiversity, including transboundary resources, creates enabling systems, incentives, and policies to facilitate private sector participation in Blue Economy business opportunities (Component 2), and establishes a regional Caribbean Blue Economy Hub to showcase, support, and regularly update information on blue business opportunities and investments that enhance conservation and sustainable use of marine and coastal ecosystems (Component 3). In addition, the project promotes socialising, scaling, and replication of the BluEFin approach through a regional community of learning on conservation finance (Component 4), and ensures efficient, gender‑responsive monitoring, reporting, and independent evaluation to support timely, adaptive implementation across all components (Component 5).

projects.name: TTO GEF Small Grants Programme 2025
projects.description:
In support of the SGP 2.0 objective to catalyze and mobilize civil society actors and local actions needed to address major drivers of environmental degradation and help deliver multiple benefits across the GEF’s mandated thematic dimensions, while promoting sustainable development and improved livelihoods, GEF SGP Trinidad and Tobago is overseeing and reporting on 13 ongoing projects from the following NGOs:
1.	Future Fishers – sustainable fisheries through conversion of by-catch into value-added products
2.	Matelot Police Youth Club (MPYC) – solarisation of the Club House to reduce vulnerabilities due to regular electricity outages 
3.	St. Mary's Police Youth Club (SMPYC) – establishment of a youth apiculture programme to prevent youth involvement in crime and increase conservation of bees
4.	Youths of Tobago – crab conservation at the Mason Hall Secondary School
5.	Tobago Reforestation and Watershed Rehabilitation Programme (TRWRP) – creation of value-added products (teas) from the Tobago reforestation programme, thereby developing a financial driver for reforestation
6.	Buccoo Reef Trust (BRT) – purchase of equipment to support the disaster responsiveness and preparedness of Tobago in partnership with Tobago Emergency Management Authority (TEMA) 
7.	Autistic Society of Trinidad and Tobago – climate smart agriculture to provide livelihood opportunities for persons with autism
8.	Digicel Foundation – implementation of the first Persons with Disabilities Innovation Challenge
9.	The UWI Life Sciences Department – development of compost and compost tea from sargassum to support agriculture and farmers.
10.	Conserving Habitats and Environmental Organisms (CHAPO) – engaging youth in the design and build of equipment to remove sargassum from the sea as well as in the development of products from the sargassum
11.	Nature Seekers – conversion of sargassum into biogas to fuel jewellery making from waste glass from Matura Beach.
12. Trinidad and Tobago Field Naturalist Club – supporting regional biodiversity conservation
13.  Grande Riviere Tourism Development Organization – solarisation of the community facility building which supports several community activities.

projects.name: JAM: Hurricane Melissa Response and Recovery
projects.description: In the Education sector, UNESCO will support schools through the provision of vital teaching and learning materials, including textbooks, while providing technical support for a comprehensive Post Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA), while rolling out mental health and psychosocial support for teachers and providing cash grants to 100 teacher-students at Sam Sharpe Teachers College. In the Culture sector,  UNESCO will conduct a training in PDNA methodology to support the recovery of the cultural sector, and provide technical assistance for the possible reconstruction of an iconic heritage building and for a structural assessment and subsequent total restoration of the Sea Wall, a component of the recently inscribed World Heritage Site of Port Royal. In the Communications and Information sector, UNESCO will conduct a PDNA of the media sector, strengthen national capacity for real-time news verification, deploy RadioBox studios, Starlink terminals and 15W FM transmitters, and strengthen data-driven disaster communication. In the Natural Sciences sector, UNESCO will conduct a rapid assessment of the island’s major scientific and research infrastructure, provide targeted financial and technical assistance to the Water Resources Authority of Jamaica for the urgent rehabilitation of critical hydrological infrastructure, and support the University of the West Indies (UWI) to implement the Women in Science Emergency (WISE) Initiative, which will provide twenty micro-grants to graduate-level women scientists whose studies and research were disrupted by Hurricane Melissa. And, in the Social and Human Sciences sector, UNESCO will strengthen the capacities of the Jamaica Council for Persons with Disabilities for inclusive disaster risk reduction while launching Resilience Labs to engage vulnerable youth and persons with disabilities in designing creative income-generating solutions.

projects.name: GLB BDS: UNFCCC 12th Umbrella biennial transparency report and national communications, BTR/NC
projects.description:
The GEF-8 #11500 Enabling Activity Global Project is assisting 8 countries including Dominica, Grenada and St. Vincent & the Grenadines in the Caribbean to fulfill essential communication requirements to the Convention and the Paris Agreement and is in conformity with Objective 2.2 of Pillar II under GEF-8 Climate Change Focal Area Strategy, that fosters enabling conditions to mainstream mitigation concerns into sustainable development strategies. The project falls under BTR1 top-up Modality 3, as described in the Information Note on the Update to the Financing of Biennial Transparency Reports for the Developing Country Parties to the Paris Agreement (GEF/C.62/Inf.15). This modality supports countries to access additional (top up) financing to ongoing enabling activity (EA) projects and is only intended to be used for their first BTRs. This option allows country teams that would have been delayed in commencing the BTR work, considering the status of NC/BUR processes, to draft and complete their NCs, BURs and BTRs concurrently.  The Project is scheduled to end 30 April 2028.

The following BTR financing arrangements and projects have been identified for the top-ups as informed by varying technical capacities and country preferences:
i) Dominica BTR1 merged with the Initial Biennial Update Report i.e. BUR1 – GEF ID. 6925
ii) Grenada BTR1 merged with the Third National Communication i.e., NC3 – GEF ID. 4794, which will result in a combined BTR1/NC3 project.
iii) Saint Vincent & the Grenadines BTR1 merged with the Third National Communication i.e., NC3 – GEF ID. 4794, which will result in a combined BTR1/NC3 project.

projects.name: Implementation Support for Water, Sanitation and Urban Infrastructure Improvements in Dutch Quarter, Sint Maarten
projects.description: The Sint Maarten Dutch Quarter Water and Sanitation project supports the rehabilitation and expansion of critical wastewater and urban infrastructure in a densely populated community. The project focuses on upgrading and completing sewerage infrastructure, including wastewater collection and conveyance systems, pumping infrastructure and connections required to improve sanitation services and reduce environmental and public health risks. Planned works include completion of the pumping station, rationalization of existing intermediate infrastructure, connection of sewerage pressure lines and the progressive establishment of residential house connections. The intervention also incorporates complementary public infrastructure improvements, including sidewalks and streetlighting, to improve accessibility and safety within the project area. projects.name: Elimination of hazardous chemicals from supply chains Integrated Programme in Trinidad and Tobago
projects.description:
The GEF-8 #11176 Project titled, “Elimination of Hazardous Chemicals from Supply Chains Integrated Programme in Trinidad and Tobago” child project is one of the eight child projects of the GEF 8 Integrated Programme (IP) 11 “Eliminating hazardous chemicals from supply chains”. The objective of the IP is to promote transformational change in the fashion and construction sectors by replacing resource-intensive processes and materials with sustainable approaches and alternatives and creating and strengthening circular and transparent supply chains.

The Project is implemented by UNEP and aims to transform the Carnival fashion sector by promoting the use of sustainable, locally sourced materials and eliminating hazardous chemicals from costume production. It addresses environmental and health risks posed by materials such as plastic beads, sequins, and metal wire frames that may contain persistent organic pollutants (POPs) and heavy metals. It also fosters gender equity by increasing women’s participation and leadership in the Carnival industry, and disseminates knowledge and practices to other global Carnival events, contributing to broader environmental and socio-economic benefits. The executing partner is the Trinidad-based, Basel Convention Regional Centre for Training and Technology Transfer for the Caribbean (BCRC-Caribbean). Total project budget is US$2,652,294 over 6 years, and the Project official end date is 31 October 2031

projects.name: REG Harnessing trade policy and transport and logistics to build sustainable and resilient food supply chains in the Caribbean
projects.description:
Objective of the Project
To strengthen the capacities of selected countries in the Caribbean and the Arab region to leverage trade policy measures and harness transport and logistic to be better prepared for and respond to supply chain disruptions and build sustainable and resilient food supply chains.

Activities
The project will enhance national actions and policy coordination by supporting the development of policies and plans that promote food security and inclusive and sustainable economic growth through sustainable and resilient food trade and food transport and logistics systems. The project will be deployed across three main phases:

Phase 1 will assess the current state of play regarding food trade and food transport and logistics systems. It will also help to identify needs and gaps as put forward context specific recommendations and solutions.

Phase 2 will focus on implementing the recommendations and solutions identified in Phase 1.

Phase 3 will aim to expand regional cooperation in the field of sustainable and resilient food trading and food transport and logistics system. This will ensure wider dissemination of the project benefits within the target regions and beyond.  Outreach and dissemination activities will include dedicated collaborative platforms, consultation mechanisms, and distance learning.

projects.description: UNDRR will continue supporting Governments in developing national disaster risk reduction strategies and action plans through an inclusive, gender- and disability-responsive and demand-driven approach. UNDRR will facilitate partnerships towards supporting the development/revision and implementation of existing disaster risk reduction strategies and track their implementation, including through the active engagement of national multi-stakeholder coordination mechanisms for disaster risk reduction. UNDRR will strengthen the leadership in disaster risk governance of women, Indigenous communities and persons with disabilities. UNDRR technical support will focus on ensuring that planners and decision makers have the required disaster risk knowledge and capacity, including a deeper understanding of the root causes of vulnerability and the gendered systemic nature of risk, and appropriate scientific evidence for effective planning, implementation and monitoring of inclusive disaster risk reduction strategies. Technical advice to Governments in reviewing existing legal and regulatory frameworks will contribute to more effective risk governance. Providing support to the development of sound monitoring, accountability and financing frameworks for national-level disaster risk reduction actions will reinforce effective roll-out and implementation of the strategies and action plans. UNDRR will also continue promoting the formalisation and strengthening of National Platforms for Disaster Risk Reduction as the governance mechanism to ensure coherence among the different policies and activities being designed and implemented by multiple sectors and actors

projects.name: REG The Smart Seas Toolkit for Disaster Resilience and Digital Inclusion project
projects.description:
The Smart Seas Toolkit (SST) for Disaster Resilience (“Smart Seas”) project is a joint initiative of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), Caribbean Telecommunications Union (CTU) and the Telecommunications Authority of Trinidad and Tobago (TATT), supported by the Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago which aims to increase the resilience and ultimately preserve the lives of Caribbean small-scale fishers (SSF) through information and communications technologies (ICTs), with emphasis on the enabling environment.

The project will identify gaps which may exist in the maritime communications enabling environment, from which gap-filling recommendations will be produced under consultation with key stakeholders within the region. These recommendations, along with other resources produced during the project, will form part of an online toolkit to strengthen the enabling environment. The project is initially being implemented in Trinidad and Tobago, which serves as the Maritime Rescue Co-ordination Centre (MRCC) for: Barbados, Grenada, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, as well as Trinidad and Tobago. The project outputs and outcomes are expected to be transferable to other Caribbean countries.

Furthermore, the project aims to facilitate the establishment of an international community to tackle the ongoing challenge of inaccessible communications at sea, through technological, service and market innovations. Subsequent phases of the Smart Seas project will introduce a certification program for marine very high frequency (VHF) radio- operation and increase SSF capacity. Later phases will also feature the utilization of cutting-edge communication technologies to close data gaps in the maritime sector that are essential for boosting resilience across the mitigation, preparation, response, and recovery phases of the disaster risk management cycle.

TTO: Purchase of Very High Frequency (VHF) Coast Station equipment for the Trinidad and Tobago Coast Guard; Digital Skills Training for the Trinidad and Tobago Coast Guard

projects.name: REG Early warning systems and anticipatory action strengthen resilience and ensure timely action to reduce the impact of disaster
projects.description:
Evidence shows that countries with multi-hazard early warning systems in place experience significantly fewer fatalities and lower economic disruption when disasters occur. The United Nations Secretary General’s call for UN member states to strengthen Early Warning Systems for All initiative (EW4All) continues to spearhead significant global progress. However, many countries still lack comprehensive systems that integrate timely hazard monitoring, effective communications to exposed people and infrastructure and services, and effective preparedness measures that reach communities at risk.

As co-lead of the EW4ALL initiative and lead on Pillar 1, Disaster Risk Knowledge for early warning systems, UNDRR will accelerate  the development of risk information and assessments to strengthen national early warning systems. By empowering countries to use risk information effectively to improve early warning systems coupled with anticipatory action it will support substantial reductions in disaster-related deaths, economic losses, and disruptions to livelihoods, resulting in stronger resilience of communities and national systems.

projects.description:

projects.description:

•	Delivery of legal support to Members States for the ratification of the San Jose Treaty, to counter maritime crime. During 2022 UNODC conducted missions to provide legal support to the beneficiary countries, including Barbados, and to secure states buy in. This activity remains ongoing in 2023. 
Development of SoP on evidence handling for operators at sea for all beneficiaries, as well as production of a report on Caribbean legislation and best practices on maritime crime. This activity was completed in 2022. 

•	Support for the improved maritime law enforcement and maritime domain awareness  capabilities through the delivery of training for in all countries, including the participation of prosecutors to ensure legal finish of all maritime crime.

•	Development of SoP on evidence handling for operators at sea for all beneficiaries, as well as production of a report on Caribbean legislation and best practices on maritime crime. This activity was completed in 2022.

projects.name: TTO UNODC Global Firearms Programme: Partner with relevant counterparts in CARICOM Member States, as well as CARICOM IMPACS, to strengthen the national legislative framework consistent with the international legal regime on firearms for a safe, secure and just society.
projects.description:
Under the UNODC Global Firearms Programme, and in close cooperation with CARICOM IMPACS, UNODC is currently implementing the Project “Support to the implementation of the crime prevention and criminal justice component of the Caribbean Roadmap to counter illicit firearms trafficking and misuse across the Caribbean in a sustainable manner by 2030”. The project is funded by Germany and aims to support the implementation of the Caribbean Roadmap in specific areas related to its crime prevention and criminal justice component and reduce the scourge of armed violence in the region. It also seeks to contribute to regional efforts to prevent and counter illicit circulation, misuse of firearms and their links to other serious crimes, in particular transnational organized crime.
 
In 2022, the Global Firearms Programme implemented the following programmes in, or with the participation of Trinidad and Tobago:

-	Legislative review assessing national legislation on firearms and organized crime in compliance with international and regional instruments, consolidated in one final report shared with the country.
-	Legal workshop with Attorney General’s Office and relevant national stakeholders to discuss results of legislative review conducted by the programme and tailor findings with their feedback.

projects.name: TTO Trinidad and Tobago E-commerce Strategy Development Project
projects.description:
The need to develop a better understanding of the interface between the digital economy and international trade is increasingly recognized. Over the last couple of decades, e-commerce has emerged as a potentially powerful driver of economic growth, inclusive trade and job-creation in the developing world. However, due to a number of economic, infrastructural, human and financial constraints associated with continuing digital divides across and within them, many developing countries are lagging behind in terms of the readiness to engage in and benefit from e-commerce and the digital economy. The UNCTAD ECDE Programme has developed its policy and technical assistance to support countries requesting assistance in building and maintaining a dynamic and responsive ICT policy environment. It helps to ensure that national ICT programmes become an instrument for supporting relevant components of the national development agenda, enabling local industry to compete in a knowledge-based, global economy, generating better paying jobs, enhancing financial inclusion and standards of living, reducing poverty, and promoting economic growth and export diversification.

Following a request by the Ministry of Trade and Industry, this project aims to develop a national E-commerce Strategy (ECS) for Trinidad and Tobago, to replace the previous strategy (2017-2021) which has come to an end. The project will be delivered under the UNCTAD E-commerce and Digital Economy (ECDE) Programme and will contribute to the efforts by the Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago (GoRTT) to use technology to accelerate change and development, including through economic diversification, job creation and increased trade. Particular focus will be devoted to supporting the use of e-commerce by local businesses to serve domestic, regional and international markets. The project will consist of 3 phases: preparatory phase (with desk review, mapping of stakeholders and dissemination of surveys), diagnostic phase (with the preparation of an eTrade Readiness Assessment that will provide an up-to-date and detailed overview of constraints and opportunities for e-commerce development in key policy areas) and ECS development phase (with the preparation of a national ECS). The project will assist the GoRTT in developing a roadmap for how e-commerce can be used to support trade and technological progress with a view to promoting a more inclusive and sustainable socioeconomic development in the country. By bringing relevant stakeholders together, the project aims to promote a coordinated, whole-of-government output based on participatory process.

projects.name: ANT & BAR: Sustainable Pathways: Protected Areas and Renewable Energy (SPPARE)
projects.description: The Sustainable Pathways: Protected Areas and Renewable Energy (SPPARE) (GEF-5, #5390) Project commenced in 2015 and encountered several delays, as well as disruption from the COVID-19 Pandemic. The Project Objective involved demonstration of an integrated and self-sustaining approach to environmental stewardship in a Small Island Developing State (SIDS) and to enhance financing and management of protected areas through innovations in renewable energy capacity in Antigua and Barbuda. The Project had 4 Components: 1) Development of Sustainable Island Resource Financial Plan - implementation of the environmental legislation and management of protected areas through the establishment of relevant strategies; the outcome is the development of the financial strategy for the implementation of the legislation and the management of protected areas. 2)  Pilot expansion of Sustainable Island Resource Protected Areas: Boggy Peak National Park (BPNP) - establishing a model-managed protected area that is sustainably managed and financed; the outcome is a model managed protected area that is financially self-sustaining. 3) Renewable Energy in support of Protected Areas Systems Pilot - installation of renewable energy technology to ultimately support the established pilot protected area; the outcome is at least 100,000 tons of CO2 equivalent emissions avoided as direct impact of the pilot with immediate plans for 1,000,000 tCO2. 4) Enhancement of Forest Systems - developing a public awareness strategy for reducing fires in forest ecosystems and establishing a carbon sink through the restoration of forested areas; the outcome is fires reduced nationwide by 20% by Project end.

projects.name: REG Advancing a Regional Approach Towards the Green Hydrogen Economy in Latin America and the Caribbean
projects.description:
The Project aims to create an enabling environment to foster the development of a regional green hydrogen economy and to build the capacity of participating countries to attract investment, develop policies, and implement strategic projects. Jamaica and Trinidad & Tobago are among seven countries in the Latin America & Caribbean region (including Bolivia, Chile, El Salvador, Honduras and Uruguay) participating in the regional initiative funded by the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and implemented by UNEP. The use of green hydrogen as an energy vector to support countries' decarbonization pathways is a genuinely new vision that was endorsed by many countries at the UNFCCC COP26 meeting.  Total regional Project budget is US$2,049,971.

As a Group A (early stage) country (including El Salvador & Honduras), the Government of Jamaica is advancing the development of a national green hydrogen economy as part of its broader transition toward a low-carbon, resilient, and diversified energy system. Green hydrogen presents a strategic opportunity to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels, decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors, strengthen energy security, and unlock new areas of industrial development and investment. To support this emerging sector in a coordinated and inclusive manner, the establishment of a National Green Hydrogen Inter-Institutional Working Group is proposed, to serve as a national advisory and coordination mechanism, bringing together key public and private stakeholders to support policy coherence, strategic planning, and informed decision-making related to green hydrogen development in the country. The national partners are the Ministry of Economic Growth and Job Creation (MEGJC), now Ministry of Economic Growth and Infrastructure Development (MEGID); Ministry of Energy, Transport & Telecommunications (METT) and the Ministry of Water, Environment & Climate Change (MWECC).

As a Group B (more advanced) country (including Chile, Bolivia, Uruguay), Trinidad & Tobago is a regional energy leader with a strong foothold in petrochemicals and strategically positioned to spearhead the development of a green hydrogen economy in the LAC region. Leveraging its existing oil and gas infrastructure, operational expertise, and favorable economic conditions, the nation can potentially transform into a green energy superpower. Trinidad & Tobago's competitive advantage includes: its energy sector contribution of 40% of GDP and 80% of export earnings; its strong heritage in oil and gas production and petrochemical exports (ammonia and methanol); its established infrastructure which offers a competitive edge in the emerging hydrogen market; the strategic positioning of the Point Lisas Industrial Estate, poised to be a regional hub for green hydrogen and downstream products; and its thriving energy ecosystem and existing markets with trade relations and export routes. Trinidad & Tobago's lead in existing infrastructure also provides a head start in the green hydrogen market. The national partner is the Ministry of Planning & Development (MPD), now the Ministry of Planning, Economic Affairs & Development (MPEAD).

projects.description:
Micro-, Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (MSMEs) account for the majority of businesses and employment globally, but often lack the resources and capacities to assess and manage disaster risks.

UNDRR will enhance business resilience, especially among MSMEs, by promoting the use of business resilience planning methods and tools such as the UNDRR Resilience Maturity Assessment (ReMA).

Through its signature engagement platforms, the Private Sector Alliance for Disaster Resilient Societies (ARISE) and the network of Chief Corporate Resilience Officers (CCROs), UNDRR will convene businesses, financial institutions, and industry associations to identify investment opportunities and align business practices with resilience objectives. 

UNDRR will develop tailored guidance and collaborate with multinational companies, business associations to enable businesses to assess disaster and climate risk and resilience gaps to develop risk-informed business continuity plans, and embed risk reduction across supply chains and in business strategies and plans.

projects.name: TTO Airport Communication Programme (AIRCOP) is a collaboration between UNODC – WCO – INTERPOL: Strengthened institutional capacities for the identification, investigation and interception of transnational organized crime at international airports.
projects.description:
As outlined in the UNODC Strategic Vision for Latin America and the Caribbean, a more harmonized approach to continue supporting Member States on the implementation of specialized cross-border approaches that have demonstrated positive results on detection and interdiction of illegal Trafficking. 
AIRCOP is a  multi agency project based on the cooperation between  UNODC,  INTERPOL and  the World Customs Organisations (WCO) that aims at  strengthening the capacities of participating  international airports in Africa, Latin America, the Caribbean and the Middle East to  detect and intercept drugs, other illicit goods (including firearms, their parts and ammunition) and high-risk passengers (including victims of trafficking in persons and foreign terrorist fighters) in origin, transit and destination countries with the overall objective of  disrupting the illegal criminal networks. 
The increased capacity and knowledge of trained personnel has led to the expansion of the project scope to cover the multiple  threats targeting airports, including all illicit drugs, illicit goods (such as wildlife, counterfeit medicines or weapons) and, as of late, terrorism and trafficking in persons.
In 2022, UNODC signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Government of Trinidad and Tobago for the implementation of the AIRCOP Programme at the Piarco International Airport in Port-of-Spain, Trinidad and Tobago. To date, 8 vetted officers from the Trinidad and Tobago Police Service (TTPS), the Immigration Department, the Customs Agency have been assigned to form the AIRCOP Task Force.
AIRCOP provides a range of standard and specialized training and mentoring activities, tailored tonational and regional needs. Topics covered include intelligence collection and sharing, targeting, search techniques, counterfeit documents, behavioral analysis, use ofl aw enforcement databases, secure communication procedures and post-seizure investigations, as well as specific thematic issues.
In 2022, UNODC facilitated training for the AIRCOP Task Force in the following areas:
-	AIRCOP Introductory Training
-	AIRCOP Training on Integrity in Law Enforcement
-	AIRCOP Training on Gender and Human Rights in Law Enforcement
-	Specialized Training on the Safe Handling of Synthetic Opiods, use of Raman Drug Testing Devices and Drug Precursor Kits
-	Specialized Training on Intelligence and Data (API and Passenger data)
-	Specialized Training on the Use of the WCO CENComm Platform
-	Exchange of Best Practices amongst AIRCOP JAITFs in Barbados, Jamaica and Trinidad and Tobago
Likewise, retrofitting and equipping of the AIRCOP working room was also carried out in 2022. One Raman Drug Testing Device was delivered to the AIRCOP Team for the Identification and Detection of Illicit Substances.

projects.name: Enhancing resilience of Suriname´s water supply system
projects.description: The national Project, "Enhance the resilience of Suriname´s water supply system by modelling drought risks and developing a roadmap of prioritized alternatives for aquifer recharge" is funded by the Climate Technology Centre and Network (CTCN) - the implementation arm of the Technology Mechanism of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, hosted by UNEP.  The primary objective of this technical assistance Project is to pinpoint areas most vulnerable to droughts and subsequent water variability and shortages through drought risk assessment and mapping. Under the Project, the Project will:  i) assess drought risk and water resources and Issue risk maps through Geographical Information Systems (GIS) software to identify the area’s most at risk of droughts; ii) map aquifers suitable for recharge; iii) design a fully integrated system that will enable Suriname to recharge its aquifer in time of drought in a sustainable, clean, and safe manner; and iv) train national officers in the use of the drought prevention model and in the designed system to manage the water resources in the aquifer in time of drought (see: https://www.ctc-n.org/technical-assistance/projects/enhance-resilience-suriname-s-water-supply-system-modelling-drought)

projects.name: TTO: Phase 0: Technical assistance for the strengthening of the Justice Sector in Aruba
projects.description: The Aruba technical assistance for strengthening the justice sector supports the Ministry of Justice in preparing the development of a new detention facility through a pre-feasibility study and the transition toward Phase 1. The project contributes to strengthening the correctional sector and national infrastructure capacity by advancing a resilient, sustainable and effective long-term facility that enables safe and humane detention and supports rehabilitation and reintegration. The four key deliverables are: a consolidated assessment and gap analysis of the existing KIA facility; a high-level prison profile defining the needs and objectives of the future facility; high-level functional programming outlining the required configuration and capacity; and a business case setting out the technical, operational and financial basis for investment. Together, these deliverables provide the Government of Aruba with the foundation to advance decision-making, mobilize resources and move into Phase 1 of the new KIA development.

projects.name: JAM: Strengthen the capacity of Jamaica’s tripartite partners in developing and adopting a National Employment Policy (NEP).
projects.description: The ILO is supporting the Government of Jamaica, through a Memorandum of Understanding with the Office of the Prime Minister, to finalise and adopt a comprehensive National Employment Policy (NEP) led by a Tripartite Steering Committee. Building on the diagnostic phase already undertaken, the intervention will deliver: (i) finalisation and validation of the NEP and its Action Plan, including a governance, results and resource framework; (ii) strengthened capacity of the technical drafting committee and key labour market stakeholders through social dialogue, advocacy and targeted capacity-building activities; (iii) integration of skills development priorities into the NEP, informed by an analysis of changing skills demand and supply and dedicated stakeholder consultations; and (iv) incorporation of updated labour market diagnostics, including a rapid assessment of the 2025 hurricane impact. The initiative aims to enhance Jamaica’s capacity to develop and implement an inclusive, resilient and evidence-based employment policy framework, contributing to full and productive employment and the achievement of SDG 8.

projects.name: TTO Towards NDC 3.0: Updating Trinidad and Tobago’s Nationally Determined Contribution Implementation and Financial Investment Plans (UNDP)
projects.description:
The joint programme titled 'Towards NDC 3.0: Updating Trinidad and Tobago’s Nationally Determined Contribution Implementation and Financial Investment Plans' aims to accelerate Trinidad and Tobago's transition to renewable energy by updating its NDC Implementation and Financial Investment Plans, fostering cross-sectoral collaboration, and enhancing capacities for climate resilience and sustainable development.

This joint program updates Trinidad and Tobago's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) Implementation and Financial Investment Plans, enhancing commitments under the Paris Agreement. It fosters cross-sectoral collaboration to reform policies, mobilize resources, and build capacities, focusing on a just energy transition across sectors, including agriculture. Key outcomes include a comprehensive NDC Implementation Plan, a refined Financial Investment Plan, and strengthened institutional capacities, directly benefiting 75 policymakers and sectoral leaders. The program supports SDG transitions in energy access, climate action, and decent jobs, positioning Trinidad and Tobago as a leader in climate resilience and sustainable development among Small Island Developing States.

projects.name: TTO Protecting the marine environment from land-based pollution through strengthened and coordinated global action - Capacity Development for Action on Plastic Pollution (CDA-PP)
projects.description:
The Project, "Capacity Development for Action on Plastic Pollution (CDA-PP)" provides capacity support to catalyze actions and commitments at the national and global level to reduce marine plastic pollution including in the marine environment.  Implementation in Trinidad & Tobago is through the Basel Convention Regional Centre for Training and Technology Transfer for the Caribbean (BCRC Caribbean) on behalf of the Ministry of Planning & Development. The Project will advance various UNEP chemicals and pollution mandates (UNEA Resolutions 1/6, 2/11, 3/7, 4/6 on plastics/marine plastic/litter/microplastics; and 5/14 - End Plastic Pollution: Towards an international, legally binding instrument) to build national capacity and advance the objectives of the Global Programme of Action for the Protection of the Marine Environment from Land-based Activities (GPA) and of the Global Partnership on Plastic Pollution and Marine Litter (GPML). The Project is part of the broader UNEP Programme of Work project 522.4 “Protecting the Marine Environment from Land-Based Pollution through Strengthened Coordination on Global Action” and contributes to Component #3 of UNEP's global "One Plastics Initiative".
Expected outputs: 1) Report on national stakeholder engagement; 2) State of Knowledge report; 3) National Source Inventory report including a legislation and policy analysis; 4) National Roadmap/Strategy/ Plan; 5) National validation process report; 6) Awareness raising communications products

projects.name: A detailed report on migrants' needs in Sint Maarten, including recommendations for the implementation of CBI responses is available through the deployment of DTM capacity in targeted locations.
projects.description:
Building on the capacities of trained partners and to inform an evidence-based understanding of humanitarian and protection needs, IOM will deploy DTM activities in selected locations, in coordination with the Government of Sint Maarten. In parallel, and to support community engagement, limited cash-based assistance may be provided to particularly vulnerable individuals identified during the data collection process. This support is intended to facilitate access to essential services and context-appropriate assistance.

Data collected will be consolidated into an analytical report outlining migrants’ social protection needs in Sint Maarten, accompanied by recommendations for addressing identified gaps through cash-based interventions. The analysis will also explore the applicability of the approach to other areas of migrant assistance, with a view to strengthening protection outcomes for vulnerable groups, including those exposed to exploitation or abuse.

projects.description: The Technology Needs Assessment Project (GEF-6 #9452) was a global support project involving involving 24 countries (Caribbean SIDS: Antigua & Barbuda, Dominica, Jamaica, Suriname & Trinidad & Tobago). The TNA Project identified and prioritised technologies for climate change mitigation and adaptation in developing countries. Technology transfer in project countries is facilitated through improved Technology Needs Assessments and provides targeted financial and technical support to prepare new or updated and improved TNAs, including Technology Action Plans (TAPs), for 9 prioritized technologies that reduce greenhouse gas emissions, support adaptation to climate change, in the agriculture and water management sectors. Countries conducted Barrier Analyses and Enabling Frameworks (BAEF) and prepared concept notes for prioritised actions (for GCF funding). Note that the Project was initially scheduled to end in 2022 but was granted extensions to 2023 (March and June variously) to allow countries (e.g. Suriname) time to complete activities.

projects.name: Stronger and Greener Productive Capacities for Just Transitions in Caribbean Small Island Developing States
projects.description:
This initiative, in collaboration with UNDESA, ECLAC and the RC system, supports four Caribbean SIDS to boost statistical capacity, identify productive capacities gaps, and design holistic programmes to address these gaps. Funding is particularly important as SIDS often have less access to external finance and are among the most indebted developing countries in the world. To address the debt problem, UN Trade and Development has advocated for a new development-centered international debt architecture. 

This means:

Scaling up concessional finance and grants from multilateral and regional development banks through greater capitalisation and re-channeling of unused Special Drawing Rights to Multilateral Development Banks.
Enhancing international liquidity through improved access to existing Global Financial Safety Net instruments with a focus on fairness and increased quotas for developing countries.
Implementing standstill rules that provide breathing space during crises to boost resilience to external crises. A good example are climate-resilient debt clauses.
Enhancing debt sustainability analysis by reflecting investments in the SDGs.
And making the Common Framework worthwhile for countries in distress

projects.description: GCF has established the Readiness and Preparatory Support Programme (RSRP) and the Project Preparation Facility (PPF) - jointly referred to as the Readiness Programme - designed with the specific aim of promoting country ownership in responding to the challenges to climate change. Since its operationalization in 2014, the Readiness Programme has been providing funding for early support activities to enhance ownership and enable access to the GCF resources. Since 2018, UNOPS has been engaged with the GCF and provided grant management support to selected proposals of the Readiness Programme. On 12 December 2020, the GCF published the RFP 2020/028 on Procurement of Grant Management Services of its RPSP and the PPF. More specifically, the RFP states that the objective of the assignment is to provide high quality GMS to support the GCF Secretariat in ensuring that approved Readiness and PPF projects are implemented in a professional, effective and efficient manner. To provide these services to the GCF Secretariat, a qualified, reputable and experienced firm/consortium is contracted for a period of up to eight years, subject to the results of a Mid-Term Evaluation after year five.

projects.name: REG Caribbean governments and other stakeholders supported to integrate climate change and disaster risk reduction into relevant strategies and policies across and within the education sector
projects.description:
UNDRR will continue to collaborate with Governments, partners, and networks through targeted and contextualized technical assistance to promote and implement comprehensive risk management governance. This will establish a shared understanding of risk as the basis for integrated implementation across timescales. 

These interventions aim at strengthening governance at the national level for the alignment of policies, practices, and knowledge related to both disaster risk and climate.

Using a package of guidelines and tools on comprehensive risk management developed during the previous biennium, UNDRR will provide technical assistance to Governments to develop and implement disaster risk reduction strategies and national adaptation plans in the context of the Country Support Approach.
 
UNDRR will assist in extending such synergy to key sectors like the education sector. In particular, support will be provided to the Caribbean Safe Schools Initiative (CSSI) and its Action Plan in accordance with the Antigua and Barbuda Ministerial Declaration of 2017 and the Sint Maarten Declaration on School Safety 2022, which reaffirms the 2017 declaration. These declarations provide key entry points for comprehensive risk management in the education sector. National and local linkages will be further strengthened through the application of the comprehensive school safety framework.

The approved work programme accords with the Multilateral Fund’s Strategic Planning and  -year Business Plan for 2021-2023. HPMP II Activities include: a) Enhance the enabling policy, legal and intuitional framework for the HCFC Phase out; b) Enforce the Licensing and quota system (LQS) and other provisions of the regulatory and
Standards framework; c) Reduce HCFC demand; d) Develop and implement a public education and awareness programme; e) Develop and implement project monitoring, evaluation and reporting to ensure the efficient and effective implementation of the HPMP Stage II. A no-cost extension is approved to 30 June 2026, with a total budget of $105,000. 1st Tranche = $81,000; 2nd Tranche = $24,000. Scheduled end date of Project is June 2027.

projects.name: TTO Towards NDC 3.0: Updating Trinidad and Tobago’s Nationally Determined Contribution Implementation and Financial Investment Plans (FAO)
projects.description:
The Joint Programme directly supports three key MSDCF Outcomes and their related Outputs. It contributes to Outcome 2 by advancing economic diversification and environmentally sustainable growth through the development of green, blue, and circular economy pathways. It supports Outcome 5 by strengthening Trinidad and Tobago’s adaptive capacity to climate change, updating the NDC Implementation Plan, and enhancing institutional readiness for a just and equitable energy transition. Under Outcome 6, the JP promotes sustainable natural resource management—particularly within the AFOLU sector—helping to build ecosystem and community resilience. In alignment with these outcomes, the JP advances Output 2.2 by supporting policy and systems development for sustainable agriculture and energy, Output 5.1 by enhancing national institutional capacity for climate adaptation and mitigation planning, and Output 6.1 by scaling up sustainable natural resource management practices that reinforce resilience across communities and ecosystems.

Output 1.1: Updated and Costed NDC Implementation Plan that Reflects the Revised Targets, Latest National and Sectoral Strategies, Perspectives of Diverse Stakeholders, and Just Transition Considerations.

•	Output 1.2: Addendum to the NDC Implementation Plan with Actionable Steps for AFOLU Inclusion.

•	Output 2.1: A Refined Financial Investment Plan that Aligns with the Updated NDC and NDC Implementation Plan (and that integrates private-sector inputs, via the Trinidad and Tobago Chamber of Industry and Commerce and the American Chamber of Commerce of Trinidad and Tobago, amongst others).

•	Output 3.1: Personnel and Institutions with Enhanced Capacity to Implement an Updated NDC and Inclusively Drive the Energy Transition.

projects.name: GUY SubOutput 7.3.1: 'Spotlight initiative' 'Partnership for Peace' - Batterer Intervention Programme
projects.description:
The Partnership for Peace (PfP) Programme is a court-based accountability programme which uses a psycho-educational approach to ensuring the prevention of continued violence against women on the part of men who are in the court system as perpetrators of domestic violence.  The Batterer Intervention programme is a standardized intervention developed by an expert group of human rights lawyers, clinical psychologists, social workers, and women’s rights advocates.
The programme is premised on basic principles that include the prioritization of the safety and protection of women victims of violence and the acknowledgement of accountability and responsibility by the perpetrator.  The key elements of the programme are:
•	Domestic abuse is conceptualized as part of “pattern of coercive control”.
•	Abuse is solely the responsibility of the perpetrator and survivors should never be blamed for abuse.
•	Counselling is not guaranteed to end the violence and that such intervention is not intended to salvage relationships.
projects.outcome: GUY Output 7.3 Support provided to strengthen mechanisms and services for women, children experiencing violence/abuse

projects.name: GUY SubOutput 8.1.3:  'Spotlight Initiative' 'Foundations Programme' - Roll out of Foundations Programme in schools and community-based settings
projects.description:
The Foundations Programme seeks to address gender based violence (GBV) through prevention and targets young persons aged 13 to 24. The Programme is built on the premise that GBV and gender discrimination are influenced by choice, fueled by gender hierarchies and unequal gender relations. The main objectives of the Foundation Programme are as follows:
1. To empower young people to understand GBV and its genesis in gender inequalities and gender-based discrimination.
2. To promote an understanding of the consequences of GBV to partner(s), children, communities and societies in general.
3. To endow young people with knowledge, skills and attitudes for addressing conflict and responding to stress and stressors that arise in relationships.
4. To establish and model an atmosphere of respect within group relations among and between young people.
5. To promote self-sufficiency among young people in taking steps towards improving their relationships and their lives.
6. To create a network of young people who will advocate for non-violent relationships.

In light of the above objectives and reaching the beneficiary population, schools and community settings in Guyana will be targeted.
