projects.name: Accelerating the transition to a net-zero, nature-positive economy in Trinidad and Tobago (TT Net-zero)
projects.description:
The project’s overall objective is to significantly accelerate the reduction of Trinidad & Tobago’s dependency on oil and gas production while contributing to a national transition towards a net-zero, nature-positive economy. This objective will be achieved through a three-fold approach.
Project activities aim to reform the national policy environment to maximize synergies between climate, biodiversity and human well-being. Hence, the Government of Trinidad and Tobago commits and takes nature-positive action to decarbonize its economy towards a net-zero target.
Also, project activities address barriers to finance such that T&T’s public and private sector will deploy financing mechanisms to mobilize investments for the decarbonization of the economy with a particular focus on the energy sector. This involves the implementation of sectoral and thematic reforms and plans for the energy sector in line with a developed NZNP strategy.
It is further envisaged that interventions will showcase the feasibility of low-carbon, nature-positive technologies by implementing NZNP-aligned demonstration projects on Trinidad as well as on the island of Tobago.
The project is expected to be transformative in supporting T&T in transitioning towards a net-zero, nature-positive economy. The project is expected to achieve greenhouse gas emissions mitigation over the project’s lifetime of 860,699 tCO2e, of which 3,320 tCO2e will be direct and 857,379 tCO2e indirect, to achieve 100 ha of land and ecosystems under restoration, 1000 ha of landscapes under improved practices, and reach 3,260 beneficiaries, with a targeted distribution of 1,630 women and 1,630 men.
projects.outcome: MSDCF 2.3: National and regional capacities strengthened to accelerate the green energy transition

projects.name: Trinidad and Tobago Open-Source Programme Office (TT-OSPO)
projects.description:
The Open-Source Programme Office (OSPO) project will support the Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence (MPA-AI) of Trinidad and Tobago in its mission to modernize government services through open-source technology, increasing efficiency and promoting inclusivity. The OSPO will strengthen the capacity of the public sector to advance the vision outlined in the National Digital Strategy (2023-2026), which prioritizes overcoming bureaucratic silos, fostering whole-of-government processes, addressing inefficiencies, and mitigating resistance to digitalization. Additionally, the OSPO will facilitate the establishment of a sustainable national ecosystem for open-source collaboration, innovation, and multi-sectoral partnerships.
This OSPO initiative aligns with UNDP’s Digital Strategy, promoting Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) as a foundation for sustainable development and inclusivity. By cultivating an open-source ecosystem, the OSPO aims to reduce Trinidad and Tobago’s reliance on proprietary software, empower government entities to innovate, and foster a digitally resilient, inclusive society where open-source tools are accessible and effectively utilized.

projects.name: REG Implementation of the Strategic Action Programme to ensure Integrated and Sustainable Management of the Transboundary Water Resources of the Amazon River Basin Considering Climate Variability and Change
projects.description:
The GEF-6 (#9770) Project is implemented in Guyana and Suriname and other member states of the Amazon Cooperation Treaty Organization (ACTO) i.e. Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela. It is implementing the agreed Strategic Action Plan (SAP) by promoting Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) and source‑to‑sea approaches that improve ecological, social and economic benefits across the basin. The Project applies basin‑wide IWRM principles to develop and strengthen a community‑to‑cabinet innovative water governance model that reinforces institutional and policy frameworks, supports the establishment of water authorities where needed, and introduces incentive‑based financing mechanisms such as water funds, green/climate bonds and payments for ecosystem services to generate long‑term support for SAP implementation (Component 1). It further builds community resilience and enhances protection of bio‑aquatic ecosystems through up‑scaled forecasting and alert systems for floods and droughts, natural infrastructure and adaptation measures in coastal and glacier‑dependent areas, and groundwater source protection solutions that reduce contamination risks in vulnerable urban centers (Component 2). In addition, the project establishes integrated, basin‑wide environmental monitoring and reporting systems for water quality, hydro‑meteorology, erosion and sediment transport, bio‑aquatic ecosystems, and priority headwater and wetland areas, providing compatible indicators and data to inform science‑policy decision‑making and reporting under the SDGs and relevant conventions (Component 3). The project also promotes long‑term sustainability of SAP implementation through a comprehensive indicator‑based monitoring and reporting framework, innovative ICT applications and web portals, and targeted communication and marketing products that facilitate knowledge sharing and stakeholder engagement at regional and national levels (Component 4). The total Project budget is $11,735,780, with Guyana and Suriname benefitting from regional scope activities.

Local implementing partners are the Guyana Ministry of Public Works and Suriname Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Business and International Cooperation (BIBIS)

projects.name: BARBADOS DECENT WORK COUNTRY PROGRAMME, 2025-2030
projects.description:
The Barbados Decent Work Country Programme (DWCP) for 2025–2030 establishes the common commitment of the Government of Barbados, employers’ and workers’ organizations, and the International Labour Organization (ILO) to promote Decent Work. It provides a strategic framework to support inclusive, resilient, and sustainable development, aligned with national priorities and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The DWCP focuses on four key priorities:

Productive employment and sustainable enterprises – Promoting job creation, entrepreneurship, and enterprise development, with emphasis on youth, women, and vulnerable groups.
Social protection – Strengthening the coverage, adequacy, and sustainability of social protection systems, and enhancing resilience to economic and climate-related shocks.
Rights at work and labour standards – Advancing compliance with international labour standards, improving working conditions, and reinforcing labour administration and inspection.
Social dialogue and tripartism – Strengthening collaboration among government, employers, and workers to support effective labour market governance and consensus-based policymaking.

Through these priorities, the DWCP aims to expand decent work opportunities, reduce inequalities, and strengthen institutional capacity in Barbados.

projects.name: 2.7.6 BDS Improved capacity of decision makers to leverage ethical artificial intelligence systems in their national decision-making policies and plans to advance safety, social cohesion and benefits across the society
projects.description:
AI Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM): Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a dynamic technology of the 4th Industrial Revolution. Its effects are forecasted to impact every aspect of society. As the discussions about AI heightens, many SIDS including those in the Caribbean, have yet to develop strategies and national policies to manage the impacts of AI on their society even as the citizens interact with AI in daily life. As an underrepresented stakeholder in the AI ethics debate, Caribbean SIDS must begin to articulate the indigenous knowledge, cultural and ethnic pluralism, and diverse value systems that define the sub-region, in line with global ethical standards.  

AI systems raise new types of ethical issues that include, but are not limited to, their impact on decision-making in employment and labour, social interaction, health care, education, media, freedom of expression, access to information, privacy, democracy, discrimination, and weaponization. Furthermore, new ethical challenges and risks are created by the potential of AI algorithms to reproduce biases, for instance regarding gender, ethnicity, and age, and thus to exacerbate already existing forms of discrimination, identity prejudice and stereotyping. As Caribbean nations expand their adoption of AI tools and other frontier technologies, stakeholders (policymakers, citizens, private sector, academia, and NGOs) must proactively collaborate to create strategies for the humanistic and ethical development and adoption of guidelines, regulations and frameworks.

projects.name: GUY SubOutput 7.1.5a: Develop capacities of relevant counterparts to target, manage risk and inspect containers for combatting the illict movement of contraband and promoting safe, secure and just trade practices at maritime ports.
projects.description:
The mission of the UNODC-WCO Container Control Programme (CCP) is to build capacity in countries seeking to improve risk management, supply chain security, and trade facilitation in seaports, airports and land border crossings in order to prevent the cross-border movement of illicit goods. The UNODC-WCO Container Control Programme (CCP) was established as a joint initiative of the UNODC and the WCO in 2004. Faced with such a complex and globalized problem, the CCP embraces a nuanced, holistic and multi-sectoral approach by providing continuous monitoring and oversight, offering a plethora of context-specific training programmes and strengthening cooperation between state agencies and with the private sector. The mission of the CCP is to build capacity in Member States seeking to improve risk management, supply chain security and trade facilitation in seaports, airports and land border crossings in order to prevent the cross-border movement of illicit goods.

At present, the CCP is operational in over 70 Member States. More than 120 Port Control Units (PCUs) and Air Cargo Control Units (ACCUs) have been established since the CCP's inception in 2004. These inter-agency units are equipped to exchange information with their counterparts in other countries using a secure communication application, developed by the WCO, called ContainerComm. This provides PCUs and ACCUs with access to a wealth of information, allowing users to share information about high-risk containers and verify their identification numbers.

The CCP Programme is currently under implementation in the Port of Georgetown in Guyana. In 2022, capacity building programmes to support enhanced profiling of containers was carried for the benefit of the PCU in Georgetown, including exchange programmes with the Port of Hamburg in Germany and other PCUs in the Caribbean basin. UNODC also provided additional of safety and search equipment to the Georgetown PCU. Study visits to Germany port of Hamburg.

projects.name: REG Strengthening national-level institutional and professional capacities of country Parties towards enhanced UNCCD monitoring and reporting (GEF-7 #10959 Umbrella III)
projects.description: The GEF-7 (#10959) Global Support Project, GSP-III, "Strengthening national-level institutional and professional capacities of country Parties towards enhanced UNCCD monitoring and reporting, Umbrella III" is an enabling activity supporting 20 countries (including Guyana and St. Vincent & the Grenadines) in their monitoring and reporting commitments to the UNCCD. Allocations per country equal $91,324 (GEF LD set aside). At COP12 (October 2015), the UNCCD agreed to integrate the SDGs and related targets into the implementation of the Convention and that SDG target 15.3/Indicator 15.3.1 can drive implementation of the UNCCD (decision 3/COP.12) per UNCCD Strategic Framework 2018-2030. COP12 endorsed the definition of land degradation neutrality (LDN) and invited Parties to (i) formulate voluntary targets to achieve LDN, (ii) use the UNCCD monitoring and evaluation framework, including progress indicators, to monitor, evaluate and communicate progress towards achieving the LDN target, (iii) explore options on how to integrate the voluntary LDN targets in their UNCCD National Action Programmes (NAPs), and (iv) promote the use of LDN targets and projects and other SLM initiatives as an effective vehicle for mobilizing additional sustainable financing and investments to address issues related to desertification, land degradation and drought (DLDD). Decision 2/COP.12 invites affected country Parties to establish national baselines and national-level voluntary LDN targets within their National Action Plans (NAPs). Countries are expected to monitor land degradation status and trends and formulate plans and policies for SLM practices, to avoid land degradation. GSP-III started in 2021 and is built upon GSP-I and GSP-II. GSP-I supported a simplification of the PRAIS reporting platform and built country capacity, while GSP-II established country reporting and monitoring systems aligned to the UNCCD strategy, 2018-2030.

projects.name: REG Governments and key stakeholders’ capacity strengthened to conduct systems-level risk assessments and analysis for risk reduction approaches and effective risk-informed decision-making
projects.description: UNDRR will support Member States and stakeholders in shifting their standard risk management frameworks from simply managing hazards to engineering an improved understanding of risk and how impacts can escalate and cascade across systems. UNDRR will do this by providing technical support to national partners and the UN system on risk information and analytics, foresight and anticipatory actions to inform decision-making. This will include supporting enhanced analytics and data aggregation efforts that take into account the complex climate future and the impacts of changes on people, planet, and prosperity. At the country level, UNDRR will deliver guidance materials, technical tools, and training on cascading, multi-hazard, and systemic risks to strengthen in-country risk assessment capability. Normative guidance, based on lessons learned, will also help inform risk reduction and climate change integration in Government plans and policies. UNDRR will strengthen risk analytics and assessment processes across the UN system, particularly in UN-coordinated planning processes such as the Humanitarian Programme Cycle and UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Frameworks, as well as national disaster risk reduction strategies and national adaptation plans. UNDRR will also support national authorities in promoting the protection of biodiversity, ecosystems, and water cycles through the reduction of disaster and climate risks. UNDRR will provide support on risk understanding to the Early Warning for All initiative. This work will strengthen and enhance national capacities to collect, analyze, access, and use disaster risk knowledge for more inclusive and accessible multi-hazard early warning systems. UNDRR will also continue implementing the roadmap developed by the Centre of Excellence that shifts the focus from responding to disasters only after they occur to making a greater investment in preventative comprehensive disaster and climate risk management. The Centre will give particular attention to areas and communities characterized by highly vulnerable and fragile contexts.

projects.name: TTO UNODC TRACK4TIP: Key institutions and relevant stakeholders are strengthened to support the enhanced identification, investigation and prosecution of cases of human trafficking, from a victim-centered approach.
projects.description:
Justice responses to combat trafficking in persons in migration flows (TRACK4TiP).

TRACK4TIP initiative is a four-year (2019-2023), initiative by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and supported by the United States Department of State. The project is being implemented and reaches eight countries across South America and the Caribbean with actions at the national and regional level among Ecuador, Peru, Brazil, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Trinidad and Tobago, Curaçao and Aruba.

TRACK4TiP aims to enhance the regional criminal justice response to human trafficking among migration flows within the beneficiary countries following a victim-centered and multidisciplinary approach working at the regional and local levels to identify, prevent and prosecute cases.

To achieve this, TRACK4TIP proposes the implementation of seven main activities organized under three specific objectives that together make it easier for each of the eight beneficiary countries to achieve the main objective of strengthening their criminal justice response in cases of trafficking in persons involving Venezuelan victims migrating in the region.

Objective 1- Capacity Building

To improve victim identification and national referral mechanisms at the country level to better identify and safely report human trafficking cases in the context of migration flows at ports of entry, transit points, and destination communities in beneficiary countries.

Activity 1
Enhancement of identification and referral mechanisms at ports of entry, transit points, and destination communities in beneficiary countries to safely report human trafficking cases.

Activity 2
A Capacity Building strategy on the use of the National Referral mechanisms to safely report human trafficking cases at ports of entry, transit points, and destination communities.

Objective 2 - Knowledge and research

Provide law enforcement and prosecuting authorities in beneficiary countries with reliable information on the modus operandi of criminal networks or individuals that are associated with human trafficking among populations migrating within the region.

Activity 3
Country narratives on the context, investigations, and prosecutions for human trafficking cases at ports of entry, transit points, and destination communities among migration flows.

Activity 4
A Sub-regional Threat Assessment on the current context, dynamics, and trends of human trafficking cases among migration flows involving Venezuelans.

Objective 3 – International Coordination and Cooperation
Promote at the national and regional level, new investigations and prosecutions for human trafficking cases among migration flow involving Venezuelans establishing liaison between National coordination mechanisms and law enforcement agencies and prosecutors with authority to investigate and prosecute TIP at beneficiary countries.

Activity 5
Promotion of current networks and task forces to enhance coordination of law enforcement agencies, prosecutors, and national coordination mechanisms.

Activity 6
Operationalization of new investigations and prosecutions through the communication channels and coordination mechanisms created by the project.

Activity 7
Tracking and monitoring information on the progress of the criminal justice response to investigate and prosecute human trafficking cases in the context of migration flows.

In 2022 in Trinidad and Tobago, TRACK 4 TiP implemented Specialized training for law enforcement officers to detect, investigate, and prosecute trafficking in persons following a victim-centered approach: The training aimed to provide TTPS officers in Trinidad & Tobago enhanced investigative techniques to strengthen the identification of TIP victims in the country. In addition, the training had a cybercrime portion to also provide new resources and information to officers on social media recruitment and online methods used for TIP.
Participating agencies included: Trinidad & Tobago Police Service, Counter Trafficking Unit and Ministry of National Security.
Likewise, TRACK4TiP also supported the design of a standardized referral form and operating procedure for the Counter Trafficking Unit. ONGOING

projects.name: TTO: Aruba - Afterschool Program: Sinja Merdia
projects.description: Operating from Monday to Thursday for two hours at the IOM Aruba office, the program includes personalized language instruction in Dutch, Papiamento, English, and other school subjects as needed, tailored to the specific needs of each child. Social workers are present during program hours, offering additional MHPSS to help the children cope with the stress of adaptation and integration. They are trained to identify emotional and psychological needs, providing one-on-one support and facilitating group activities that promote social and emotional well-being. This holistic approach not only focuses on language acquisition but also on fostering a sense of belonging and resilience among the children. By combining educational and psychosocial support, the program helps young learners thrive in their new community, opening doors to future opportunities and empowering them to fully participate in their academic and social environments. Additionally, the program offers CBI to the most vulnerable migrant families participating, helping them with school and insurance fees.

projects.name: TTO: Aruba - Nourish and Thrive
projects.description:
Food Assistance for Vulnerable Migrants: This activity provides vital food assistance to refugees, migrants, and affected host community members, ensuring access to nutritious meals during times of need. By addressing immediate hunger and food insecurity, the program supports the health and resilience of vulnerable populations, fostering community stability and well-being.
Nutrition Workshops: This program offers nutrition workshops led by a certified nutritionist, designed for refugees and migrants. Additionally, the program will accept referrals from IOM’s free clinic for individual counseling. The classes focus on practical, culturally sensitive guidance to improve health and well-being. Participants learn about balanced diets, food security, and how to manage limited resources for better nutrition. By addressing the specific needs of each family, the program supports healthier lifestyles and contributes to long-term well-being and integration. Participants in need of food assistance will be referred to IOM.

projects.name: REG Local governments develop, finance and implement multi-hazard climate- and nature-sensitive resilience plans
projects.description:
UNDRR will strengthen the capacity of local governments to design, finance, and implement multi-hazard resilience plans that are climate- and nature-sensitive, ensuring that risk reduction is embedded across local development processes. To do this, we will leverage UN system expertise including joint programming on local resilience to accelerate efforts to support local risk governance. UNDRR will provide risk governance and resilience tools to help subnational entities assess gaps, integrate resilience into budgetary systems and plan improvements across the disaster risk management spectrum.

Working with city networks and regional partners, UNDRR will expand the reach of the Making Cities Resilient 2030 initiative (MCR2030), supporting local authorities to move from planning to implementation. This includes providing guidelines and training packages, diagnostics, and methodologies that help local governments operationalize risk reduction measures and track progress in building resilience. UNDRR’s guidance and tools will also extend to the preparation of investment-ready proposals addressing disaster risk reduction and climate action needs and on the application of AI and geospatial solutions in local risk assessment, scenario modelling and investment planning.

projects.name: BZE 8.2.3 Capacities enhanced in support of meaningful youth engagement to promote inclusive and peaceful ​Caribbean SIDS.
projects.description:
Young people in the Caribbean have a significant contribution to make to promoting sustainable development. Creating an environment that is conducive and supportive of youth-led action and youth participation contributes to overall positive social development in the sub-region. 

Young people have been significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, exacerbating pre-existing vulnerabilities derived from increased inequalities of income and opportunity. Nevertheless, despite these difficulties, youth have been at the forefront, helping their communities overcome challenges caused by the pandemic. SHS supports countries in the Caribbean to prioritize actions and policies that build on the potential of youth and address their needs to allow them to exercise their rights.
This sub-outputs aims at: 
- Strengthened capacities of public officials from CARICOM Member States to apply the principles of meaningful youth engagement in programming and policy. 
- Joint action plan developed to advance the YPS agenda in the English and Dutch-speaking Caribbean. 
- Coordination mechanism created to follow-up on this action plan, including considering the launch of a YPS regional coalition. 
- Strengthened Network of Directors for improved knowledge sharing and exchange on youth engagement. 
-Strengthened capacities of Caribbean youth-led organizations on gender equality and advocacy by developing tools for young people to develop their own project ideas and drive social change in their communities.
projects.outcome: MSDCF 8.1: Government and civil society capacities are strengthened to advocate for, implement and monitor efforts to challenge harmful social norms, and build and maintain safer, fairer, more inclusive, and equitable societies

To build awareness and foster synergy between policies and practices for the protection of culture from the effects of disasters trough capacity building, awareness raising and advocacy in the Caribbean SIDS. The activity will help to identify ways in which workflows for risk reduction, emergency preparedness and response for the culture sector can be incorporated within the national/local disaster risk reduction and emergency management.

The Caribbean Plan of Action for Disaster Resilience and Recovery of the Culture Sector (2023-2033) constitutes a specific agenda geared towards supporting disaster resilience and recovery in the culture sector, through awareness-building, capacity-building, institutional strengthening, policy and legislation, promoting synergies and best practices across the region, and strengthening coordination between disaster, climate change and culture actors at the national level, and culture NGOs, UNESCO, CARICOM and CDEMA at the regional level.

projects.name: GBL: Institutional capacity enhanced to adopt and act on national and international commitments (Support for the Preparation of the Fourth National Biosafety Reports to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety)
projects.description: This global Project (GEF-5 #5688) provided support to eligible parties for GEF funding in order to sustain and build capacity for effective participation in the Biosafety Clearing House (BCH) in line with COP/MOP Decisions, specifically BS VI/5 para 2f. It aims to ensure (i) that participating countries have established sustainable national procedures to gather information to put on the BCH, and (ii) that they have the expertise to use, access and participate efficiently to the BCH. This will ultimately improve countries’ compliance to the Protocol while ensuring a safer handling and use of LMOs for a further Global Conservation of Biodiversity. 7 Caribbean countries benefited from Project activities: The Bahamas, Barbados, Grenada, Dominica, Jamaica, Suriname and Trinidad & Tobago. The Project experienced several delays in contract agreements and disruption from the COVID 19 Pandemic, which required received several Project extensions.

projects.name: TTO UNODC Global Programme on Money Laundering: Member States have increased capacity to identify, investigate and prosecute money laundering, including Trade Based Money Laundering
projects.description:
The UNODC Global Programme against Money Laundering, Proceeds of Crime and Financing of Terrorism (GPML), with the financial support of the Government of Canada, is implementing a three-year capacity building programme on trade-based money laundering (henceforth referred to as ‘the Programme’) for 13 beneficiary countries in the Caribbean and Central America. 

The goals of the Programme are to (i) raise awareness of the public security threats stemming from TBML and (ii) strengthen the capacities of law enforcement and prosecutorial authorities to detect, investigate and prosecute money laundering through trade more effectively. The Programme comprises a series of capacity building activities – national and regional workshops, free trade zones (FTZ) training, development of TBML e-learning modules, and mentoring. 

Based on the findings from the initial fact-finding exercise and the scoping missions conducted in the beneficiary countries in 2019, UNODC GPML developed the concept & methodology paper to deliver the TBML national workshops in Central America and the Caribbean. According to the latter, UNODC GPML adopted a twofold approach for the national TBML workshops: 
i	building capacities through the simulation of a real-life TBML case, and 
ii	presenting the relevant techniques, tools and methods contextualised in the case scenario, which allow the participants to learn and use them more effectively. 
Based on the goals and adopted approach of the Programme, the objectives of the national TBML workshops are as follows: 

•	Provide the participants with the understanding, knowledge and tools required to identify, investigate, and prosecute TBML. 
•	Show the importance of national and international cooperation and coordination for the effective detection, investigation, and prosecution of TBML. 
•	Identify the principal sources of information required for the detection, investigation, and prosecution of TBML. 
•	Link the financial investigation parallel to the criminal investigation to cut the illicit benefits generated from money laundering and its predicate offences. 
•	Build capacities through a learning-by-doing methodology by simulating a real-life TBML case. 

In 2022, GPML provided training to 27 practitioners from Law Enforcement Agencies in Trinidad and Tobago including: Customs, the Financial Intelligence Units (FIUs), Trinidad and Tobago Police Service (TTPS), Revenue Administration, intelligence authorities, and the Offices of the Directors of Public Prosecutions on the identification and investigation of trade-based money laundering.

projects.description: In 2023, a stock-taking analysis that was conducted to review existing national competency frameworks related to digital competencies of teachers across the 20 Caribbean countries served by UNESCO Kingston Office, assessing the extent to which they were aligned with UNESCO ICT Competency Framework’s components. The present activity aims to subsequently develop a regional roadmap and guidelines for an effective and relevant integration of the UNESCO ICT competency framework in national frameworks in those countries in order to strengthen teachers’ ICT and competencies and skills. The idea is to offer countries a more comprehensive set of competencies and skills that teachers need to integrate ICT into their professional pedagogies and practices in order to facilitate students’ achievement of curricular objectives. projects.name: Creating new jobs and livelihoods through cooperative development
projects.description:
Guyana has a long history of cooperativism, dating back to the post-emancipation period, and was declared the world’s first Cooperative Republic in 1970. While the cooperative sector expanded significantly in the 1970s, it declined due to economic challenges, institutional constraints, and skills shortages.

There is renewed national interest in cooperatives and the broader Social and Solidarity Economy (SSE) as a pathway to promote rural development, productivity, and formalization. In response, the Ministry of Labour has requested ILO support to strengthen the cooperative sector.

The intervention focuses on enhancing institutional capacity, supporting enabling frameworks, and promoting sustainable cooperative development to reduce rural isolation and improve livelihoods.

projects.name: JAM Governments assess, strengthen, and institutionalize their readiness for resilient recovery to build back better
projects.description:
UNDRR will help strengthen the role of the International Recovery Platform, the global hub for advocacy for resilient recovery, in order to identify gaps and constraints experienced in post disaster recovery and to serve as a catalyst for the development of tools, resources, and capacity for resilient recovery.

UNDRR, in collaboration with the International Recovery Platform and its partners, will support countries in assessing and strengthening their readiness for resilient recovery. Through a Recovery Readiness Assessment Framework and coordinated technical assistance, UNDRR will help countries identify gaps, prioritize improvements, and develop readiness strategies to institutionalize policies, coordination, resourcing, and capacities before disaster strikes. This work will support the integration of assessment findings and lessons learned into national systems and policies, including pre-agreed governance, institutional, and financing arrangements for post-disaster response and recovery.  UNDRR will foster peer learning and exchange to strengthen recovery efforts such as scenario-based recovery plans embedding building back better and inclusive approaches. 

In partnership with humanitarian and emergency response actors, UNDRR will support the implementation of recovery readiness assessments in fragile and humanitarian settings, where disasters can be especially devastating. UNDRR will support after-action reviews to capture lessons learned, enhance understanding of underlying vulnerability and exposure, assess recovery effectiveness and inform investments in preparedness and anticipatory action.

projects.name: REG Monitoring of Sendai Framework implementation and disaster losses generate policy insights and strengthened accountability
projects.description:
UNDRR will strengthen Sendai Framework monitoring by helping Member States improve disaster data reporting through the Sendai Framework Monitor and related SDG indicators. It will build national capacity to produce high-quality, disaggregated data across all seven Sendai targets and five disaster-related SDGs.

To support policy and planning, UNDRR will produce global, regional, and national snapshots showing progress in areas like risk governance, financing, early warning, and cooperation. These will be compared with disaster impact trends to highlight resilience gaps.

UNDRR will also help develop better data standards and methodologies, including through the global Disaster-Related Statistics Framework, to improve disaster data quality, consistency, and use for evidence-based decisions. 

UNDRR will support the rollout of an enhanced disaster tracking system – DELTA Resilience (Disaster and hazardous events, losses and damages tracking & analysis), in partnership with UNDP and WMO, to replace the existing DesInventar with a more comprehensive and interoperable tracking system that will cover both hazardous events, as well as disaggregated losses and damages at localized scales. The open-source tool uses updated standards to assess economic and non-economic impacts of extreme and slow-onset events. 

UNDRR will assist countries in institutionalizing the system and building capacity to link physical parameters to observed effects. This will support decision-making across disaster risk reduction functions, from risk analysis and early action to financing and progress tracking.

The Ministry of Health (MOH), in partnership with the National AIDS Coordinating Committee (NACC), UNAIDS, and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), is advancing efforts to strengthen Human Resources for Health (HRH) systems to sustain and enhance the HIV response in Trinidad and Tobago. The integration of HIV and STI services requires a robust HRH framework to ensure sufficient, well-trained, and equitably distributed health personnel to meet national needs to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.

projects.name: Guidelines for the transition of adolescents and youth living with HIV from Paediatric Sites to Adult services supported by a transitioning plan and peer groups for HIV and STIs
projects.description:
Adolescents continue to be affected by HIV and STIs.  In addition to challenges with new infections, transition of patients, aged 10 to 24 years, is also associated with periods of treatment default. In Trinidad and Tobago, in 2022 there were an estimated 235 adolescents with HIV aged 15–24 years old and 40 adolescents aged 0-14 on ART with viral suppression of 77% and 100% respectively. 

 While significant improvements have been made in treatment access and reduced deaths among PLHIV, certain vulnerabilities of adolescence and youth affect their ability to remain on antiretroviral medication, maintain a suppressed viral load. The evidence informed management of all aspects of transition can significantly decrease the loss to follow up for certain clients.  

In fiscal 2024/2025, the Ministry of Health, through HACU, undertook an assessment, with support from I-TECH, to look at the challenges in adolescent care and inform a standardised mechanism to support the retention in care of the adolescent population at adult HIV treatment and care sites in Trinidad and Tobago. This project being executed by the NACC Secretariat is the follow up to the assessment completed by HACU in order to include some of the social issues and complete the development of a guideline.

projects.name: REG: Symposium on Statistics for Poverty Reduction in the Caribbean
projects.description: The Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC), United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), Caribbean Development Bank (CDB), World Bank (WB), the independent non-profit KoboToolbox, and the Sir Arthur Lewis Institute of Social and Economic Studies (SALISES) of the University of the West Indies jointly convened the Symposium on Statistics for Poverty Reduction in the Caribbean, in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago on Friday 17th October 2025, also in hybrid format. projects.name: TTO Technical support in establishing a National Spatial Data Infrastructure (NSDI) in Trinidad and Tobago.
projects.description: A robust National Spatial Data Infrastructure (NSDI) is a necessary component for enhancing capabilities in spatial data management, improving, and strengthening decision-making and response mechanisms that support sustainable development. It fosters data accessibility, interoperability, reliability, and currency across all sectors of society. A comprehensive situational analysis is essential to understanding the current state, existing challenges, and opportunities within a nation's spatial data landscape, which paves the way for the development of a robust NSDI. The Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago, through the Ministry of Land and Legal Affairs (MLLA), requested technical support from the Economic Commission of Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC) to establish an NSDI that aligns with global standards and best practices. This technical service included a comprehensive situational and gap analysis for the MLLA and its agencies and provide a roadmap (including timelines) for advancing on the achievement of an NSDI with the MLLA as the lead national body.

The Project is a partnership between the European Commission, the Secretariat of the African, Caribbean and Pacific group of states (ACP), the United Nations Environment Programme and the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations. The aim is to empower key stakeholders to address environmental challenges and improve environmental management at the national and regional levels.  The first two Project phases focused on capacity capacity building activities for regional inter-governmental organisations, governments and stakeholders, who have been equipped with the appropriate knowledge and tools to i) participate in international negotiations (i.e. Conventions of Parties); ii) mainstream MEAs commitments into national policies; iii) develop environmental legislation and management tools that serve the implementation of MEAs commitments; and iv) ensure monitoring and reporting of the implementation of MEAs and on the impact of these efforts on the environment in their respective territories.  The objective of this third phase of the ACP MEAs programme is to enhance the mainstreaming and implementation of biodiversity and chemicals and waste MEAs with a focus on: i) the mainstreaming of biodiversity in agriculture, ii) the management of chemicals and waste (including hazardous pesticides), iii) the reinforcement of compliance and enforcement measures and iv) the strengthening of the implementation of regional seas conventions in ACP countries.  There were no national allocations for Caribbean countries.
